review_scope: Reviewed all 8 sparse contact-sheet pages covering 179 frames sampled every 45 seconds and all 33 dense contact-sheet pages sampled every 10 seconds. This remains a still-frame visual screening, not continuous audiovisual verification.

observations.description: Mikey appears alone at the desk while a large phone-chat panel occupies the right side; a persistent female cutout graphic and QR/contact graphic also appear.
The opening chat includes profile/face photographs and short messages; visible identities are blurred only partially in the contact sheet.
The conversation shows multiple blue voice-message bubbles, stickers, photos, and video thumbnails. These are repeatedly referenced while Mikey speaks.
Embedded images include what appears to be a vehicle dashboard/price display, outdoor/vehicle scenes, group photos, and other media used inside the conversation chronology.
A long light-background chat with many stickers, short alternating messages, and voice entries spans much of the middle of the video; sender side and sequence are visually meaningful.

A black/red media thumbnail is followed by a blue voice-call card/control that remains visible for an extended stretch from about 69:50. The control is part of the chat history and does not prove an active call, playback, or speaker identity.
The chat changes to several voice bubbles and a longer text message block, followed later by a very long scrolling message-thread overview.
The final section shows a tall overview of a long chat and then a dark chat containing photos and video/image thumbnails, including apparent public-place scenes.

dense_review_windows.reason: Opening private chat includes faces, voice messages, media, and possible travel/transaction evidence; read sequence and distinguish Mikey's commentary from source material.
Rapidly changing decorated chat thread with many short messages and stickers; sparse samples cannot preserve sender order or omitted messages.
Media preview, voice/call control, photos, and continuing chat may contain played third-party audio and claimed results.
The same phone evidence remains on screen for a long interval; denser review should verify scrolling, hidden context, and any change in displayed source.
Multiple voice messages and longer text blocks require sequential screen capture plus audio alignment.
Final long-thread overview and dark chat with embedded media require dense capture through the last sampled frame at 133:30.

attribution_limits: The studio speaker is visually consistent with Mikey, but every chat bubble, image, voice message, and embedded video belongs to a source conversation unless separately verified.
The female cutout and QR/contact graphic are overlays and do not indicate a live co-speaker.
Voice-message bubbles and call/media controls do not prove that audio was played or identify the speaker; continuous audiovisual alignment is required.
The batch metadata marks this item as a possible duplicate of mikey-youtube-video-003/efyqkeWyhUw; visual similarity alone must not grant independent source weight.
Case events, consent/refusal, and outcomes cannot be inferred from isolated screen captures without the missing messages and Mikey's audio framing.
privacy_or_third_party_risks: The private chat contains participant avatars, face photos, messages, timestamps, voice recordings, and media thumbnails.
Travel, vehicle, location-like, group-photo, and public-place imagery may identify third parties or reveal sensitive context.
The female cutout and QR/contact overlay involve third-party likeness or promotional identifiers.
Any formal reuse should de-identify chat participants and avoid reproducing private media unless authorization and necessity are established.

dense_observations.description: The opening white chat shows third-party face photographs and short alternating messages while Mikey is the only live studio person visible. The female image and QR/contact block are persistent overlays, not live participants.

From about 18:20 the chat displays face photos, multiple blue voice-message bubbles, stickers, and alternating sender sides. The ten-second sequence improves ordering but cannot identify voice speakers or prove playback.

Around 24:40 Mikey holds up another phone with an incoming- or active-call-like interface; shortly afterward the main panel shows a vehicle dashboard/price-like image and vehicle or outdoor media. The sampled visuals do not identify the caller or establish a live audible call.

Around 54:50 onward the chat includes blurred media thumbnails, photographs, and at about 68:50 a vertical video preview containing a woman's face. These are third-party materials and no statement can be attributed from the preview alone.

From about 69:50 through roughly 100:00 a blue voice-call card/button remains displayed beneath a black/red thumbnail. Its persistence indicates a static chat-history item, not visual evidence that a call is currently connected or being played.

Around 102:15 the panel switches to another white chat containing short voice-message bubbles, text blocks, and small video thumbnails. Sender-side changes are visible, but identities, audio, and any agreement or refusal require audiovisual checking.

At about 124:50 the display changes to a dark chat with green and grey sender sides and several third-party photos or video thumbnails, including apparent shop or public-place scenes, continuing to the end.

remaining_visual_limits: The dense review samples one still every 10 seconds; it is not continuous audiovisual verification and may miss brief taps, message transitions, or media playback between samples.
Voice-message bubbles, call-like interfaces, and the long blue voice-call card do not establish an active call, audible playback, speaker identity, or consent.
Much of the chat text is small, blurred, decorated, or cropped; exact wording, omitted messages, and sender identity cannot be recovered reliably from these sheets.
No refusal, agreement, behavioral result, or causal outcome is visually proven by the sampled frames alone, and third-party previews must not be treated as Mikey's statements.
